strings.name: Jennifer Doudna
strings.summary: Building on RNA structure and catalysis research, Doudna developed programmable CRISPR-Cas9 DNA cutting with Emmanuelle Charpentier and their teams. They shared the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. At Berkeley she promotes genomic research and applications and participates in ethical debates about human genome editing. Clinical therapies involve contributions from many research and medical teams.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: CRISPR-Cas9 method
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: The 2012 collaboration demonstrated reprogrammable DNA cutting, widely influencing biological experiments.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Research and translation
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Through the Innovative Genomics Institute, promotes genome editing, applied collaborations and public discussion.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Team reported VIPR research
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Team papers examined DNA-targeting mechanisms linked to CRISPR origins; this is fundamental research.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Shared the chemistry Nobel
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Awarded with Charpentier for developing a method for genome editing.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Founded a genomics platform
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Helped establish the collaboration that later became the Innovative Genomics Institute.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Published joint CRISPR-Cas9 research
strings.timeline.event-04.text: The team showed that designed RNA could guide Cas9 to cut a selected DNA sequence.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Joined UC Berkeley
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Moved from Yale to Berkeley to continue studying RNA and molecular mechanisms.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Established a Yale laboratory
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Joined Yale University to study RNA structure and function.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Earned a Harvard doctorate
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Completed doctoral research in Jack Szostak’s laboratory before postdoctoral work.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Graduated from Pomona
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Earned a chemistry degree and then entered graduate study at Harvard.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in Washington
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Grew up in Hilo, Hawaii, before pursuing biochemistry.
